- When sentiment is negative (especially strong or sustained), model tends to overcorrect downward — reduce forecast bias by 5–10% below historical mean.
- After sharp price spikes, model often overshoots and fails to correct — cap forecast peak at 1.5x prior high or adjust downward by 3–5% of spike magnitude.
- If sentiment is positive and price is trending up, model frequently overestimates — apply downward bias of 2–4% for 3–5 days post-spike.
- Mean reversion is overestimated in short-term forecasts — for 30d horizon, cap forecast at 1.2x recent 10d average if sentiment is neutral or mildly positive.
- When sentiment is volatile or mixed, model exhibits lag — delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 days if sentiment shifts sharply.
- If sentiment is consistently negative over 5+ days, model underestimates true downside — add 2–3% buffer to forecast to account for sentiment-driven risk.
